tasks.title: Position error from geometry
tasks.statement: The range error to a satellite (UERE) is **{u} m**, HDOP = **{h}**. Estimate the horizontal position error (m, 1σ).
tasks.solution: σ_hor ≈ HDOP · σ_UERE: the geometry multiplies the measurement error. The same receiver next to a house wall with HDOP 3 is three times as wrong as in the open.

tasks.title: Error from an uncompensated delay
tasks.statement: The vehicle flies at **{v} m/s**, and a GPS delay of **{d} ms** is not accounted for in the EKF. How far behind is the position (m)?
tasks.solution: During the delay the vehicle travels v·t. Hence `GPS1_DELAY_MS`: the EKF matches the measurement against a past state, not the current one.

tasks.title: Receiver clock error in meters
tasks.statement: The receiver clock has drifted by **{dt} µs** from GPS system time. What range error (km) would this cause if Δt were not the fourth unknown?
tasks.solution: Range error = c·Δt. 1 µs is 0.3 km, 1 ms is 300 km. That is why the receiver estimates Δt together with x, y, z and needs at least 4 satellites; in step 1 the clock is recovered with an error of 1–67 ns.

tasks.title: Post-correlation SNR
tasks.statement: The input signal power is **{p} dBm** and the coherent integration time is **{T} ms**. Find the post-correlation signal-to-noise ratio (dB): C/N0 = P + 174 (dB-Hz), SNR = C/N0 + 10·lg(T).
tasks.solution: The input bandwidth does not affect the post-correlation SNR: the noise after the correlator is set by the 1/T bandwidth. For −128.5 dBm and 1 ms: C/N0 = 45.5 dB-Hz, SNR = 45.5 − 30 = 15.5 dB; 20 ms adds another +13 dB (28.5 dB).
